sentences.en: I live with my family in a <mark>four-bedroom apartment</mark>.
sentences.ko: 나는 가족과 함께 방 4개짜리 아파트에서 살고 있습니다.
sentences.guide: I live with my FAMily / in a four-bedroom aPARTment.
sentences.tip: [연음] live with ➔ [리브-위드] | [강세] FAM-i-ly (1음절), four-bedroom, a-PART-ment (2음절 강세)

sentences.en: I like <mark>watching movies</mark>, <mark>going to parks</mark>, and <mark>listening to music</mark>.
sentences.ko: 나는 영화 보기, 공원 가기, 음악 듣기를 좋아합니다.
sentences.guide: I like WATCHing movies ↗, / GOing to parks ↗, / and LIS-tening to music ↘.
sentences.tip: [나열 억양] A↗, B↗, and C↘ 끝만 내려 읽기 | [묵음] listening에서 t는 묵음 [리스닝]

sentences.en: I enjoy <mark>walking and running</mark> at the <mark>waterfront park</mark> every weekend.
sentences.ko: 나는 매주 주말 수변 공원에서 걷고 달리는 것을 즐깁니다.
sentences.guide: I enjoy WALKing and RUNning / at the WAterfront park / EVery weekend.
sentences.tip: [연음] walking and ➔ [워킹앤] | [강세] WA-ter-front (앞음절 강세) | walking and running으로 발음이 훨씬 쉬워짐

sentences.en: I prefer <mark>staying home</mark> and listening to <mark>quiet music</mark>.
sentences.ko: 나는 집에서 머물며 잔잔하고 조용한 음악을 듣는 것을 선호합니다.
sentences.guide: I prefer STAYing home / and LIS-tening / to QUIet music.
sentences.tip: [발음] staying home ➔ [스테잉 홈] | [묵음] listening에서 t는 묵음 [리스닝] | [연음] quiet music [콰이어트 뮤직]

sentences.en: I love going to concerts and watching live shows.
sentences.ko: 나는 콘서트에 가고 라이브 공연 보는 것을 좋아합니다.
sentences.guide: I love GOing to CONcerts / and WATCHing LIVE shows.
sentences.tip: [발음] live는 형용사이므로 [리브❌ ➔ 라이브⭕] | concerts는 [칸-서-ㄹ츠]

sentences.en: <mark>Well, speaking of my favorite park</mark>, there is a lovely <mark>waterfront park right near my place</mark>.
sentences.ko: 음, 제가 가장 좋아하는 공원에 대해 말하자면, 우리 집 바로 근처에 어여쁜 수변 공원이 있습니다.
sentences.guide: Well, / SPEAKing of my favorite park, / there is a LOVEly waterfront park / RIGHT near my place.
sentences.tip: [구어 빈출] near my place는 집 근처를 말할 때 90% 이상 쓰임 | [연음] speaking of ➔ [스피킹-오브], right near ➔ [롸잇-니어]

sentences.en: It's pretty long, and it <mark>goes for about 5 kilometers</mark> along the water.
sentences.ko: 꽤 길고, 물길을 따라 약 5킬로미터 정도 이어져 있습니다.
sentences.guide: It's PRETty long, / and it GOES for about / FIVE kiLOMeters / a-LONG the water.
sentences.tip: [발음] goes for about ➔ [고우즈 퍼 어바웃]으로 stretches for보다 혀가 훨씬 편함 | [강세] ki-LOM-e-ters [킬-라-미터즈]

sentences.en: <mark>You know</mark>, I visit this park <mark>every single weekend to go jogging</mark>.
sentences.ko: 있잖아요, 나는 달리기를 하러 매주 주말마다 이 공원을 찾습니다.
sentences.guide: You know, / I VISit this park / EVery single weekend / to go JOGging.
sentences.tip: [호흡] You know 뒤에서 0.5초 뜸들이기 | every single weekend를 한 덩어리로 리듬감 있게

sentences.en: A <mark>round trip</mark> usually takes me about an hour, and it's a <mark>perfect workout for me</mark>.
sentences.ko: 왕복으로 보통 1시간 정도 걸리는데, 저에게 정말 딱 맞는 완벽한 운동입니다.
sentences.guide: A ROUND trip / usually TAKES me about an hour, / and it's a PERfect WORKout for me.
sentences.tip: [발음] perfect workout ➔ [퍼-펙트 워크-아웃] | takes me about an hour를 끊김 없이 한 덩어리로 발음

sentences.en: <mark>What I love most about this park is that</mark> there are lots of <mark>pretty flowers and green trees</mark> along the path.
sentences.ko: 이 공원에서 제가 가장 좋아하는 점은 산책로를 따라 예쁜 꽃들과 푸른 나무들이 참 많다는 것입니다.
sentences.guide: What I LOVE most about this park is that / there are LOTS of pretty FLOWers / and GREEN trees / a-LONG the path.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] lush trees 대신 green trees를 써서 발음 걸림돌 제거 | [연음] lots of ➔ [랏츠-오브]

sentences.en: Because the scenery is so nice, running there <mark>never gets boring at all</mark>.
sentences.ko: 풍경이 너무 멋지기 때문에, 거기서 달리는 것은 전혀 지루하지 않습니다.
sentences.guide: Because the SCENery is so nice, / running there / NEVer gets BORing / at ALL.
sentences.tip: [발음] scenery ➔ [씨-너-리] | [연음] at all ➔ [애-톨 / 애-롤]

sentences.en: <mark>So, thanks to this park</mark>, I can <mark>keep running every weekend</mark> and <mark>stay healthy</mark>.
sentences.ko: 그래서 이 공원 덕분에 주말마다 계속 달리기를 하고 건강을 유지할 수 있습니다.
sentences.guide: So, THANKS to this park, / I can KEEP RUNning every weekend / and STAY HEALTHy.
sentences.tip: [리듬] keep running [킵-러닝] ➔ stay healthy [스테이-헬씨] 간결하고 전달력 높은 2박자 호흡

sentences.en: It's definitely my favorite spot in my neighborhood.
sentences.ko: 단언컨대 우리 동네에서 제가 가장 좋아하는 장소입니다.
sentences.guide: It's DEFinitely / my FAvorite spot / in my NEIGHborhood.
sentences.tip: [발음] definitely ➔ 데피니틀리❌ [데-퍼-늣-리⭕ (t소리 탈락)] | neighborhood [네이버-훗]

sentences.en: <mark>Well, speaking of my bedroom</mark>, it's definitely my favorite space in the house.
sentences.ko: 음, 제 침실에 대해 말하자면, 집에서 단연 제가 가장 좋아하는 공간입니다.
sentences.guide: Well, SPEAKing of my BEDroom, / it's DEFinitely my FAvorite space / in the house.
sentences.tip: [강세] BED-room, FA-vor-ite | definitely는 1음절 [데-]에 강세

sentences.en: I have a <mark>king-size bed</mark>, and right next to it, there's a small table to <mark>charge my phone and smartwatch</mark>.
sentences.ko: 킹사이즈 침대가 있고, 바로 옆에는 핸드폰과 스마트워치를 충전할 수 있는 작은 테이블이 있습니다.
sentences.guide: I have a KING-size bed, / and RIGHT next to it, / there's a SMALL TAble / to CHARGE my phone and smartwatch.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] to charge my phone ➔ [투 차-지 마이 폰]으로 명사 나열보다 훨씬 자연스러움

sentences.en: <mark>What's really cool is that</mark> my room light has a <mark>ceiling fan</mark>, and I <mark>control it with a remote</mark>.
sentences.ko: 정말 멋진 것은 방 조명에 실링팬이 달려 있고, 리모컨으로 조작한다는 점입니다.
sentences.guide: What's REALly cool is that / my room light HAS a CEILing fan, / and I conTROL it / with a reMOTE.
sentences.tip: [문장 분리] 수동태를 없애고 control it with a remote로 능동 발화 | [강세] con-TROL, re-MOTE (2음절 강세)

sentences.en: Thanks to the ceiling fan, my room stays <mark>very cool in the summer</mark> even <mark>without an extra fan</mark>.
sentences.ko: 실링팬 덕분에 선풍기가 따로 없어도 여름에 방이 매우 시원하게 유지됩니다.
sentences.guide: THANKS to the ceiling fan, / my room stays VEry COOL in the summer / even withOUT an EXtra fan.
sentences.tip: [발음] without an extra fan ➔ [위다웃 언 엑스트라 팬] standing fan보다 발음이 매끄러움

sentences.en: Also, the light <mark>turns on automatically every morning</mark>, which helps me wake up right away.
sentences.ko: 또한 매일 아침 조명이 자동으로 켜져서 바로 기상하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
sentences.guide: Also, the light TURNS ON / autoMATically every morning, / which helps me WAKE UP / right aWAY.
sentences.tip: [연음] turns on ➔ [턴-존], wake up ➔ [웨이-껍], right away ➔ [라이-러-웨이] | auto-MAT-ically

sentences.en: <mark>Another great thing is that</mark> I have an <mark>attached bathroom</mark> in my room.
sentences.ko: 또 다른 좋은 점은 방 안에 전용 욕실이 있다는 것입니다.
sentences.guide: aNOTHer great thing is that / I have an atTACHED BATHroom / in my room.
sentences.tip: [연음] have an ➔ [해-번] | [발음] attached bathroom ➔ [어-태취-뜨 배쓰룸]

sentences.en: Even when I wake up early to take a shower and get ready for work, <mark>I don't wake up anyone else</mark>.
sentences.ko: 아침 일찍 일어나 샤워하고 출근 준비를 해도 다른 식구들을 깨우지 않습니다.
sentences.guide: Even when I WAKE up EARly / to TAKE a shower and get ready for work, / I DON'T WAKE up / ANYone else.
sentences.tip: [구어 빈출] disturb my family 대신 wake up anyone else ➔ [웨이껍 애니원 엘스]로 원어민다운 표현

sentences.en: Sometimes while I'm sleeping, my <mark>cats sneak into my room</mark> and sleep right between my legs.
sentences.ko: 가끔 자고 있을 때 고양이들이 방으로 몰래 들어와 내 다리 사이에서 자곤 합니다.
sentences.guide: Sometimes while I'm sleeping, / my CATS SNEAK into my room / and SLEEP / right beTWEEN my legs.
sentences.tip: [연음] sneak into ➔ [스니-킨-투] | [강세] SNEAK(살금살금 들어오다), be-TWEEN

sentences.en: They are super cute, but <mark>sometimes I wake up in the middle of the night</mark> because <mark>I feel too hot!</mark>
sentences.ko: 녀석들이 너무 귀엽지만, 가끔 밤중에 너무 더워서 깨기도 합니다!
sentences.guide: They are SUper cute, / but SOMEtimes I wake up / in the MIDdle of the night / because I FEEL TOO HOT!
sentences.tip: [속도감] occasionally ➔ sometimes로 전환하여 머뭇거림 방지 | [연음] middle of the night [미들-오브-더-나잇]

sentences.en: <mark>So, all in all</mark>, my bedroom is <mark>super comfortable and convenient</mark> for my daily life.
sentences.ko: 그래서 전반적으로 제 침실은 제 일상생활에 정말 편안하고 편리합니다.
sentences.guide: So, ALL in ALL, / my bedroom is SUper COMFortable / and conVENient / for my DAILy life.
sentences.tip: [핵심발음] comfortable ➔ 컴포터블(4음절❌) [컴프-터-블(3음절⭕)] | con-VEN-ient [컨-비-니언트]

sentences.en: <mark>Well, as I mentioned before</mark>, I usually go to the <mark>waterfront park near my house every single weekend</mark>.
sentences.ko: 음, 아까 말씀드렸듯이, 저는 보통 매주 주말마다 집 근처 수변 공원에 갑니다.
sentences.guide: Well, / as I MENtioned before, / I USual-ly GO to the waterfront park / near my house / EVery single weekend.
sentences.tip: [발음] I tend to visit ➔ I usually go to [아이 유절리 고우 투]로 직관적 발화

sentences.en: <mark>First of all</mark>, before heading out, I put on my running shoes and <mark>grab my wireless earbuds and smartwatch</mark>.
sentences.ko: 우선, 밖으로 나가기 전에 러닝화를 신은 뒤 무선 이어폰과 스마트워치를 챙깁니다.
sentences.guide: FIRST of all, / before HEADing out, / I PUT ON my running shoes / and GRAB my WIREless EARbuds and SMARTwatch.
sentences.tip: [연음] First of all ➔ [퍼스-터-볼], heading out ➔ [헤딩-아웃], put on ➔ [푸-톤]

sentences.en: <mark>Once I get to the park</mark>, I run the trail all the way and back — a <mark>round trip of about 10 kilometers</mark> in total.
sentences.ko: 일단 공원에 도착하면, 산책로를 끝까지 달리고 돌아옵니다 — 왕복 총 약 10킬로미터입니다.
sentences.guide: Once I GET to the park, / I RUN the trail / ALL the way and BACK — / a ROUND TRIP of about TEN kiLOMeters in total.
sentences.tip: [연음] Once I ➔ [원-사이], get to ➔ [겟-투], trip of about ➔ [트리-퍼-바웃]

sentences.en: <mark>Right after running</mark>, I <mark>walk for about 5 minutes to catch my breath</mark>, and then I head back home.
sentences.ko: 달리기를 마친 직후에는 가쁜 숨을 고르기 위해 약 5분간 걸은 다음 집으로 돌아옵니다.
sentences.guide: RIGHT after RUNning, / I WALK for about FIVE MINutes / to CATCH my breath, / and then I HEAD back home.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] walk for about 5 minutes ➔ [워크 퍼 어바웃 파이브 미닛츠]로 간결화 | catch my breath [캐치 마이 브레스]

sentences.en: <mark>All in all</mark>, this running routine is the <mark>perfect way to kick off my weekend</mark> and stay healthy.
sentences.ko: 전반적으로, 이 달리기 루틴은 주말을 활기차게 시작하고 건강을 유지하는 완벽한 방법입니다.
sentences.guide: ALL in ALL, / this RUNning routine / is the PERfect way / to KICK OFF my weekend / and STAY HEALthy.
sentences.tip: [연음] kick off ➔ [키-코프: 활기차게 시작하다] | [강세] PER-fect, HEAL-thy

sentences.en: <mark>Well, whenever I want to relax at home</mark>, listening to music is my <mark>favorite thing to do</mark>.
sentences.ko: 음, 집에서 편하게 쉬고 싶을 때마다 음악을 듣는 것이 제가 가장 좋아하는 일입니다.
sentences.guide: Well, / whenEV-er I want to reLAX at home, / LIS-tening to music / is my FAvorite thing to do.
sentences.tip: [구어 전환] unwind ➔ relax, go-to routine ➔ favorite thing to do로 자연스럽고 확실한 표현

sentences.en: <mark>First off</mark>, I change into comfortable clothes and <mark>turn on my Bluetooth speaker</mark> in my bedroom.
sentences.ko: 우선, 편안한 옷으로 갈아입고 내 방에 있는 블루투스 스피커를 켭니다.
sentences.guide: FIRST off, / I CHANGE into COMFortable clothes / and TURN ON my BLUETOOTH speak-er / in my bedroom.
sentences.tip: [연음] First off ➔ [퍼스-토프], turn on ➔ [터-논] | clothes는 [클로-즈]

sentences.en: <mark>After that</mark>, I usually lie down on my king-size bed and <mark>play some calm acoustic music</mark>.
sentences.ko: 그 후에 저는 보통 킹사이즈 침대에 누워 잔잔한 어쿠스틱 음악을 재생합니다.
sentences.guide: AFter that, / I usually LIE down on my king-size bed / and PLAY some CALM / a-COUS-tic music.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] play a playlist of soft ➔ play some calm [플레이 썸 캄]으로 입술 피로도 제거 (calm에서 l은 묵음)

sentences.en: <mark>So, to wrap it up</mark>, listening to music at home really helps me <mark>relax and recharge my batteries</mark> after a long week.
sentences.ko: 그래서 마무리하자면, 집에서 음악을 듣는 것은 긴 한 주를 보낸 후 편히 쉬고 재충전하는 데 큰 도움이 됩니다.
sentences.guide: So, / to WRAP it up, / listening to music at home / really HELPS me reLAX / and reCHARGE my BATteries / after a LONG week.
sentences.tip: [리듬] de-stress보다 relax가 호흡하기 편함 | recharge my batteries [리차-지 마이 배터리즈] 2박자 강세

day4.title: Day 4: 과거 경험 (15km 조깅 & YB 락콘서트)

sentences.en: I remember one <mark>really memorable experience</mark> at the waterfront park near my house.
sentences.ko: 집 근처 수변 공원에서 있었던 정말 기억에 남는 경험이 하나 있습니다.
sentences.guide: I re-MEMber / one REALly MEMorable experience / at the WAterfront park / near my house.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] particularly [파-티큘러리] 삭제하고 really [리얼리]로 교체하여 발음 정확도 향상

sentences.en: It was about <mark>six months ago on a Sunday morning</mark> — I headed out for my usual weekend jog along the waterfront trail.
sentences.ko: 약 6개월 전 일요일 아침이었어요 — 평소처럼 수변 산책로를 따라 주말 조깅을 하러 나갔습니다.
sentences.guide: It was about SIX months aGO / on a SUNday morning — / I HEADed out / for my USual weekend JOG / along the waterfront trail.
sentences.tip: [연음] headed out ➔ [헤-디-다웃] | [강세] U-su-al [유-주얼]

sentences.en: At some point, I <mark>saw a new path I'd never seen before</mark>, so I decided to check it out and <mark>ran for about 15 more minutes</mark>.
sentences.ko: 어느 순간 이전에 본 적 없는 새로운 길을 발견했고, 확인해 보기로 마음먹고 약 15분을 더 달렸습니다.
sentences.guide: At some point, / I SAW a NEW path / I'd NEVer seen before, / so I decided to CHECK it out / and RAN for about 15 more minutes.
sentences.tip: [구어 빈출] check it out [체키라웃] 원어민 최빈출 표현 | I'd never seen before [아이드 네버 씬 비포어]

sentences.en: But on the way back, I <mark>took a wrong turn</mark> and ended up <mark>getting totally lost</mark>.
sentences.ko: 그런데 돌아오는 길에 어쩌다 길을 잘못 들어 완전히 길을 잃어버렸습니다.
sentences.guide: But on the WAY back, / I TOOK a wrong turn / and ended up GETting TOtal-ly LOST.
sentences.tip: [발음 & 리듬] took a wrong turn [툭 어 롱 턴] ➔ getting totally lost [게팅 토탈리 로스트] 4박자 리듬

sentences.en: I kept <mark>running around trying to find my way</mark>, and before I knew it, I had run a total of <mark>15 kilometers</mark>.
sentences.ko: 계속 길을 찾으려고 이리저리 뛰어다녔고, 어느새 총 15킬로미터를 달려 있었습니다.
sentences.guide: I KEPT RUNning a-ROUND / trying to FIND my way, / and be-FORE I KNEW it, / I had run a TOtal of 15 kiLOMeters.
sentences.tip: [속도감] find my way back 대신 find my way로 축약하여 간결화 | before I knew it [비포 아이 뉴 잇]

sentences.en: My legs were <mark>completely exhausted</mark> after that, and I <mark>had to walk the rest of the way home</mark>.
sentences.ko: 그 이후로 다리가 완전히 녹초가 되어서, 나머지 길은 걸어서 집에 돌아와야 했습니다.
sentences.guide: My legs were comPLETEly exHAUSTed after that, / and I HAD to WALK / the REST of the way home.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] completely gave out ➔ completely exhausted [컴플리틀리 이그조스티드]로 친숙한 발음 사용

sentences.en: It was the <mark>first time in my life</mark> that I had ever run 15 kilometers — even if it was by accident.
sentences.ko: 비록 우연이었지만, 15킬로미터를 달린 건 살면서 처음 있는 일이었습니다.
sentences.guide: It was the FIRST TIME in my life / that I had EV-er run 15 kiLOMeters — / even if it was by ACcident.
sentences.tip: [연음] time in my ➔ [타이-민-마이], if it was ➔ [이-핏-워즈] | [강세] AC-ci-dent [액-씨-던트]

sentences.en: Strangely, that experience gave me <mark>real confidence</mark> — I thought, if I can run 15k by mistake, I could actually <mark>do a half marathon</mark> someday.
sentences.ko: 신기하게도 그 경험이 진짜 자신감을 주었어요 — 우연히 15km를 달릴 수 있다면, 언젠가는 하프 마라톤도 해낼 수 있을 거라 생각했습니다.
sentences.guide: STRANGEly, / that experience gave me REAL CONfidence — / I thought, / if I can run 15k by misTAKE, / I could actually DO a half MARathon someday.
sentences.tip: [구어 표현] complete 대신 do a half marathon으로 가볍고 자연스럽게 발화 | 15k [피프틴 케이]

sentences.en: Actually, I have a really <mark>memorable experience</mark> related to music — it was a rock concert I attended <mark>before I got married</mark>.
sentences.ko: 사실 음악과 관련해 아직도 기억에 남는 경험이 하나 있어요 — 결혼 전에 참석했던 락 콘서트입니다.
sentences.guide: ACTually, / I have a REALly MEMorable experience / re-LATed to music — / it was a ROCK CONcert / I atTENDed before I got MARried.
sentences.tip: [강세] ACT-u-al-ly, re-LAT-ed, at-TEND-ed | concert [칸-서-ㄹ트]

sentences.en: Back then, I went to see <mark>Yoon Do-hyun Band live</mark> with my girlfriend — <mark>who is now my wife</mark>.
sentences.ko: 그 당시, 저는 지금의 아내가 된 여자친구와 함께 윤도현 밴드 라이브 공연을 보러 갔습니다.
sentences.guide: BACK then, / I went to see Yoon Do-hyun Band LIVE / with my GIRLfriend — / who is NOW my wife.
sentences.tip: [문장 구조 개선] 복잡한 삽입절을 뒤로 빼서 말하기가 10배 수월해짐 | [강세] LIVE [라이브]

sentences.en: We were <mark>standing right next to the speakers</mark>, so the music was <mark>crazy loud</mark> — you could feel it in your chest.
sentences.ko: 스피커 바로 옆에 서 있었기 때문에 음악이 정말 미친 듯이 컸어요 — 가슴으로 진동이 느껴질 정도였습니다.
sentences.guide: We were STANDing right next to the SPEAKers, / so the music was CRAzy LOUD — / you could FEEL it in your chest.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] standing seats 대신 were standing | crazy loud rock 대신 crazy loud [크레이지 라우드]로 발음 완벽 해결

sentences.en: The whole crowd was <mark>singing along passionately</mark> to every single song, and the energy in the venue was just electric.
sentences.ko: 관중 전체가 모든 노래를 열정적으로 따라 불렀고, 공연장 안의 에너지가 정말 전기가 흐르는 것 같았습니다.
sentences.guide: The WHOLE CROWD / was SINGing aLONG PASsionately / to EVery single song, / and the ENergy in the venue / was JUST eLEC-tric.
sentences.tip: [연음] singing along ➔ [씽-잉-어-롱] | [강세] PAS-sion-ate-ly [패-셔-넛-리], e-LEC-tric

sentences.en: At that moment, it felt like <mark>everyone in the venue — thousands of complete strangers — had all become one</mark>.
sentences.ko: 그 순간, 공연장 안의 모든 사람들 — 수천 명의 완전한 낯선 이들이 — 모두 하나가 된 것 같은 느낌이 들었습니다.
sentences.guide: At THAT MOment, / it FELT like EVeryone in the venue — / THOU-sands of comPLETE STRANgers — / had ALL beCOME ONE.
sentences.tip: [연음] thousands of ➔ [싸우-전-저브] | [강세] complete strangers [컴-플릿 스트레인-저스]

sentences.en: It was such an <mark>unforgettable memory</mark>, not just because the music was amazing, but because <mark>I shared that moment with my wife</mark>.
sentences.ko: 음악이 훌륭했을 뿐만 아니라 그 순간을 아내와 함께 나눌 수 있었기에 정말 잊을 수 없는 추억이었습니다.
sentences.guide: It was such an unforGETtable MEMory, / not just because the MUsic was aMAZing, / but because I SHARED that MOment / with my WIFE.
sentences.tip: [문장 간소화] the person who later became my wife ➔ with my wife로 핵심만 깔끔하게 전달

day5.title: Day 5: 해외 여행 (일본 온천 가족여행 & 렌트카)

sentences.en: In my family, we have a yearly tradition: <mark>my mother, my sisters, and I</mark> take a trip abroad for <mark>my mother's birthday</mark>.
sentences.ko: 우리 가족에게는 연례 전통이 있습니다: 어머니 생신 때마다 어머니와 누나, 여동생, 그리고 제가 함께 해외여행을 떠납니다.
sentences.guide: In my family, / we have a YEARly traDItion: / my MOther, my SISters, and I / take a TRIP a-BROAD / for my MOther's BIRTHday.
sentences.tip: [호흡 조절] 콜론(:) 자리에서 한 번 끊고 말하기 | older/younger sister 대신 my sisters로 묶어 발음 피로 감소

sentences.en: <mark>To be honest</mark>, I don't really like long flights because they're exhausting, but <mark>Japan is great because the flight is so short</mark>.
sentences.ko: 솔직히 말해서, 비행기를 오래 타는 것은 지쳐서 별로 안 좋아하지만, 일본은 비행시간이 아주 짧아서 참 좋습니다.
sentences.guide: To be HONest, / I don't really like LONG flights / because they're exHAUSTing, / but JaPAN is great / because the FLIGHT is so short.
sentences.tip: [발음] exhausting [이그-조-스팅] | I'm not a big fan of flying보다 I don't really like long flights가 즉각 발화됨

sentences.en: Just this past spring, the four of us traveled to Japan, and we stayed at a wonderful <mark>traditional accommodation with a hot spring</mark>.
sentences.ko: 바로 지난 봄에 우리 넷은 일본으로 여행을 다녀왔고, 온천이 딸린 멋진 전통 숙소(료칸)에 머물렀습니다.
sentences.guide: Just this PAST SPRING, / the FOUR of us traveled to Japan, / and we STAYED at a WONderful / traDItional accommoDAtion / with a HOT SPRING.
sentences.tip: [연음] four of us ➔ [포-러-버스], stayed at a ➔ [스테이-대-러] | accommodation [어-카-머-데이-션]

sentences.en: What made it so relaxing was that <mark>delicious local meals were served right at the hotel</mark>, so we didn't have to look for restaurants.
sentences.ko: 특히 편안했던 점은 호텔에서 맛있는 현지 식사가 나와서 식당을 찾아다닐 필요가 없었다는 것입니다.
sentences.guide: What made it SO reLAXing was that / deLIcious LOcal meals / were SERVED right at the hoTEL, / so we didn't have to LOOK for RESTaurants.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] authentic meals were fully provided at the lodging ➔ local meals were served right at the hotel로 난이도 대폭 하향

sentences.en: Our daily routine was just perfect — <mark>I went for a refreshing morning jog</mark>, we did some sightseeing during the day, and then <mark>soaked in the hot spring after dinner</mark>.
sentences.ko: 우리의 하루 일과는 정말 완벽했습니다 — 저는 아침에 상쾌하게 조깅을 했고, 낮에는 가족들과 관광을 즐겼으며, 저녁 식사 후에는 따뜻하게 온천욕을 즐겼습니다.
sentences.guide: Our daily routine was JUST PERfect — / I went for a reFRESHing MORning JOG, / we did some SIGHTseeing during the day, / and then SOAKED in the hot spring / after dinner.
sentences.tip: [연음] soaked in ➔ [쏘-킨: 몸을 푹 담그다] | [강세] re-FRESH-ing, SIGHT-see-ing

sentences.en: <mark>Best of all</mark>, my mother loved every single moment of it, which made the whole trip <mark>deeply meaningful for all of us</mark>.
sentences.ko: 무엇보다도 어머니께서 모든 순간을 너무나 좋아하셔서, 우리 가족 모두에게 정말 깊은 의미가 있는 여행이 되었습니다.
sentences.guide: BEST of all, / my mother LOVED EVery single moment of it, / which made the whole trip / DEEPly MEANingful / for ALL of us.
sentences.tip: [연음] Best of all ➔ [베스-터-볼], moment of it ➔ [모-먼-터-빗], all of us ➔ [올-러-버스]

sentences.en: Whenever we prepare for a trip, <mark>my sisters and I split up the work</mark> so everything goes smoothly.
sentences.ko: 여행을 준비할 때마다, 모든 일이 순조롭게 진행되도록 누나, 여동생과 제가 일을 분담합니다.
sentences.guide: WhenEV-er we prepare for a trip, / my SISters and I SPLIT up the work / so EVerything goes SMOOTHly.
sentences.tip: [구어 빈출] divide up the roles ➔ split up the work [스플릿 떱 더 워크] 입에 착 붙는 원어민 회화 표현

sentences.en: For our trip to Japan, <mark>my older sister booked the hotel</mark>, and <mark>my younger sister took care of the flight tickets</mark>.
sentences.ko: 일본 여행 때 누나는 호텔을 예약했고, 여동생은 비행기 표를 담당했습니다.
sentences.guide: For our trip to Japan, / my older sister BOOKED the hoTEL, / and my younger sister TOOK CARE of / the FLIGHT TICKets.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] booked the accommodations (8음절 지옥) ➔ booked the hotel [북 타월 호텔] 3음절로 축소

sentences.en: <mark>My job was renting a car</mark> and getting an <mark>international driver's license</mark> in advance so we could travel comfortably with my mother.
sentences.ko: 제 역할은 어머니를 모시고 편안하게 이동할 수 있도록 렌트카를 예약하고 미리 국제운전면허증을 발급받는 것이었습니다.
sentences.guide: My JOB was RENTing a car / and GETting an in-ter-NAtional DRIver's LIcense in advance / so we could TRAVel COMfort-ably / with my mother.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] permit [퍼밋] 대신 한국인에게 친숙한 driver's license [드라이버스 라이선스] 사용

sentences.en: When I started driving in Japan, <mark>the steering wheel was on the right side</mark> and we had to drive on the left, so <mark>it took some time to get used to</mark>.
sentences.ko: 일본에서 운전을 시작했을 때, 한국과 달리 운전석이 오른쪽에 있고 좌측통행을 해야 해서 적응하는 데 시간이 좀 걸렸습니다.
sentences.guide: When I STARted DRIVing in Japan, / the STEERing wheel was on the RIGHT side / and we had to DRIVE on the left, / so it TOOK SOME TIME / to get USED TO.
sentences.tip: [연음] was on the ➔ [워-존더], drive on ➔ [드라이-본] | [숙어] get used to [겟 유스-투: 익숙해지다]

sentences.en: At first, I had to concentrate really hard, but <mark>once I got the hang of it</mark>, having a rental car made our trip <mark>incredibly convenient</mark>.
sentences.ko: 처음에는 엄청 집중해야 했지만, 일단 손에 익고 나자 렌트카가 있어서 여행이 믿을 수 없을 만큼 편리해졌습니다.
sentences.guide: At FIRST, / I had to CONcentrate REALly HARD, / but ONCE I got the HANG of it, / having a rental car / made our trip / inCREDibly conVENient.
sentences.tip: [연음/핵심] once I got the hang of it ➔ [원사이 갇더 행-어-빗: 감을 잡다] 한 번에 연결!

sentences.en: We were able to visit hidden scenic spots and travel at our own pace <mark>without worrying about buses or trains</mark>.
sentences.ko: 우리는 버스나 기차 걱정 없이 아름다운 숨은 명소들을 방문하고 우리만의 속도로 여행할 수 있었습니다.
sentences.guide: We were Able to VISit / HIDden SCEnic spots / and TRAVel at our OWN pace / withOUT WORrying about BUSes or trains.
sentences.tip: [발음 개선] without the hassle of public transit ➔ without worrying about buses or trains로 에세이 어투 탈피

sentences.en: <mark>Thanks to our teamwork and the rental car</mark>, it turned out to be one of the smoothest and most enjoyable family trips we've ever had.
sentences.ko: 3남매의 팀워크와 렌트카 덕분에 지금까지 다녀온 가족 여행 중 가장 매끄럽고 즐거웠던 여행 중 하나가 되었습니다.
sentences.guide: THANKS to our TEAMwork and the rental car, / it TURNED OUT to be / ONE of the SMOOTHest / and MOST enJOYable family trips / we've EV-er HAD.
sentences.tip: [연음] turned out to be ➔ [턴-다웃-투-비], one of the ➔ [워-너브-더], ever had ➔ [에-버-해드]

sentences.en: <mark>Well, when it comes to my days off or weekends</mark>, I usually like to <mark>keep a healthy daily routine</mark>.
sentences.ko: 음, 쉬는 날이나 주말에 대해 말씀드리자면, 저는 보통 건강한 하루 일과를 유지하는 것을 좋아합니다.
sentences.guide: Well, / when it COMES to my DAYS off or weekends, / I usually like to KEEP a HEALTHy DAIly rouTINE.
sentences.tip: [자연스러운 발화] holidays 대신 days off, productive 대신 daily routine으로 친숙한 단어 활용

sentences.en: Even on holidays, I <mark>wake up around 8 AM</mark>, have a <mark>light salad and yogurt</mark>, and head over to the waterfront park to <mark>go jogging</mark>.
sentences.ko: 휴일에도 8시쯤 일어나서 간단한 샐러드와 요거트를 챙겨 먹은 후, 근처 수변공원에 조깅을 하러 갑니다.
sentences.guide: EVen on holidays, / I WAKE UP around eight a.m., / have a LIGHT SAlad and YO-gurt, / and HEAD OVER to the waterfront park / to GO JOGging.
sentences.tip: [연음] wake up around ➔ [웨이-커-퍼-라운드], head over ➔ [헤-도버] | salad [샐-러드], yogurt [요-거-ㄹ트]

sentences.en: After getting back from the run, I <mark>take a refreshing shower</mark> and enjoy a <mark>delicious lunch with my family</mark>.
sentences.ko: 달리기를 마치고 돌아온 뒤에는 시원하게 샤워를 하고 식구들과 함께 맛있는 점심을 먹습니다.
sentences.guide: After getting BACK from the run, / I take a reFRESHing SHOWer / and enjoy a deLIcious LUNCH / with my FAM-i-ly.
sentences.tip: [발음] refreshing [리-프레-싱: 상쾌한] | delicious [디-리-셔스] | family [패-밀리 (3음절)]

sentences.en: In the afternoon, I relax in my room to <mark>watch some movies</mark> or <mark>spend an hour or two studying English</mark>.
sentences.ko: 오후에는 방에서 편안하게 영화를 보거나, 한두 시간 정도 영어 공부를 하며 시간을 보냅니다.
sentences.guide: In the AFternoon, / I reLAX in my room / to WATCH some MOVies / or spend an HOUR or TWO / STUDYing ENGlish.
sentences.tip: [연음] hour or two ➔ [아워-러-투: 한두 시간] | [강세] ENG-lish (앞음절 강세)

sentences.en: In the evening, I usually <mark>order some delicious delivery food</mark> for dinner and <mark>spend time relaxing with my cats</mark>.
sentences.ko: 저녁에는 보통 맛있는 배달 음식을 시켜 먹고, 고양이들과 함께 뒹굴거리며 쉬는 시간을 보냅니다.
sentences.guide: In the evening, / I usually ORder some deLIcious deLIvery food for dinner / and SPEND time reLAXing / with my CATS.
sentences.tip: [어휘] delivery food [딜리버리 푸드] | spend quality time 대신 spend time relaxing으로 간소화

sentences.en: <mark>So, to wrap it up</mark>, spending a peaceful day off like this really helps me <mark>de-stress and fully recharge my batteries</mark> for the upcoming week.
sentences.ko: 그래서 결론을 짓자면, 이렇게 평화로운 휴일을 보내는 것은 스트레스를 풀고 다가오는 한 주를 위해 에너지를 100% 재충전하는 데 큰 도움이 됩니다.
sentences.guide: So, to WRAP it up, / SPENDing a PEACEful day off like this / really HELPS me de-STRESS / and FULly reCHARGE my BATteries / for the UPcoming week.
sentences.tip: [마무리 표현] to wrap it up ➔ [투 래-피-덥] | [숙어] recharge my batteries ➔ [리-차-ㄹ지 마이 배-터-리즈]

sentences.en: Hey Min-su, it's Hyuk! <mark>Do you have a minute to talk?</mark> I was wondering if you're <mark>free this Saturday morning</mark>.
sentences.ko: 민수야 안녕, 나 혁이야! 잠깐 통화할 시간 돼? 이번 주 토요일 아침에 시간 괜찮은지 궁금해서 전화했어.
sentences.guide: Hey Min-su, / it's Hyuk! / Do you have a MINute to talk? / I was WONdering / if you're FREE this Saturday morning.
sentences.tip: [전화 오프닝] Do you have a minute to talk? [두유해버-미닛투-톡] | I was wondering if ~ [아이워즈-원더링-이프: ~인지 궁금해서]

sentences.en: You know the <mark>waterfront park near my place</mark>? The weather is supposed to be amazing, so I was thinking of going there for a <mark>light jog and a walk</mark>.
sentences.ko: 우리 집 근처 수변 공원 알지? 날씨가 정말 좋을 거라고 해서, 가볍게 조깅도 하고 산책이나 하러 갈까 생각 중이었거든.
sentences.guide: You know the WAterfront park near my place? / The WEATHer is supposed to be aMAZing, / so I was thinking of going there / for a LIGHT JOG and a walk.
sentences.tip: [제안 표현] I was thinking of ~ing [아이워즈-띵킹-오브: ~할까 생각 중이었어] | supposed to be [서포우스-투비: ~하기로 되어 있다]

sentences.en: <mark>What time works best for you?</mark> <mark>Around 9 or 10 in the morning</mark> would be okay?
sentences.ko: 몇 시에 만나는 게 제일 편해? 아침 9시나 10시쯤 괜찮을까?
sentences.guide: WHAT TIME works best for you? / Around NINE or TEN in the morning would be okay?
sentences.tip: [시간 묻기] What time works best for you? [왓타임 웍스 베스-포유: 언제가 제일 편해?] | ~ would be okay? [~ 우드비 오케이?: ~면 괜찮아?]

sentences.en: Also, after running, <mark>how about grabbing some brunch</mark> or a <mark>cup of coffee nearby</mark>?
sentences.ko: 그리고 달리기 끝나고 나서, 근처에서 브런치 먹거나 커피 한잔하는 건 어때?
sentences.guide: Also, AFter running, / HOW aBOUT grabbing some brunch / or a CUP of COFfee nearby?
sentences.tip: [캐주얼 제안] grab brunch/coffee [그랩 브런치 / 컵 오브 커피: 간단히 먹다/마시다] | How about ~ing [하우 어바웃 ~잉]

sentences.en: Oh, and <mark>should I pick you up</mark>, or do you want to <mark>meet directly at the park entrance</mark>? Give me a call back, okay? Bye!
sentences.ko: 아, 그리고 내가 너 데리러 갈까, 아니면 공원 입구에서 바로 만날래? 전화 줘, 알았지? 안녕!
sentences.guide: Oh, and SHOULD I PICK you up, / or do you want to MEET diRECTly / at the PARK ENtrance? / GIVE me a call back, okay? Bye!
sentences.tip: [원어민 표현] pick you up in my car에서 군더더기 in my car 삭제 | pick you up [피큐업]

sentences.en: Hey Min-su, it's Hyuk again. <mark>I'm really sorry, but something unexpected just came up</mark> and <mark>I don't think I can make it</mark> to the park tomorrow morning.
sentences.ko: 민수야, 나 혁이야. 정말 미안한데 갑자기 예기치 못한 일이 생겨서 내일 아침에 공원에 못 갈 것 같아.
sentences.guide: Hey Min-su, it's Hyuk again. / I'm REALly SORry, / but something unexPECTed just came up / and I DON'T think I can make it / to the park tomorrow morning.
sentences.tip: [문제 발생 필수 표현] something unexpected just came up [썸띵 언익스펙티드 저스트 케임업] | I don't think I can make it [메이킷: 가다/참석하다]

sentences.en: My mother just called and <mark>asked me to help her with something urgent</mark>, so I have to go over there.
sentences.ko: 방금 어머니한테 전화가 왔는데, 급한 일이 생겨서 좀 도와달라고 하셔서 거기에 다녀와야 할 것 같아.
sentences.guide: My mother just called / and ASKED me to HELP her / with SOMEthing URgent, / so I HAVE to GO over there.
sentences.tip: [구어 빈출] urgent family errand ➔ something urgent [썸띵 어-전트]로 직관적 발화

sentences.en: I feel so bad about this! First of all, <mark>are you free on Sunday morning instead</mark>? The weather looks great on Sunday as well.
sentences.ko: 정말 미안해! 우선 혹시 대신 일요일 아침에 시간 돼? 일요일도 날씨가 아주 좋다고 해.
sentences.guide: I feel SO BAD about this! / First of all, / ARE you FREE / on SUNday morning inSTEAD? / The WEAther looks GREAT on Sunday as well.
sentences.tip: [친구 톤] Would you be available 대신 Are you free? [아 유 프리]로 자연스러운 롤플레이 톤 완성

sentences.en: If Sunday doesn't work for you, <mark>how about meeting up late tomorrow afternoon</mark> around 5 PM after I finish my errand?
sentences.ko: 만약 일요일이 안 된다면, 내일 볼일을 다 마친 후 늦은 오후 5시쯤 만나는 건 어때?
sentences.guide: If Sunday doesn't work for you, / HOW aBOUT meeting up / LATE tomorrow AFternoon around 5 p.m. / after I finish my errand?
sentences.tip: [대안 2 제안] If ~ doesn't work for you [이프 ~ 더즌 웍 포유: ~가 안 된다면] | late afternoon [늦은 오후]

sentences.en: <mark>Either way, lunch and coffee are on me</mark> to <mark>make it up to you</mark>! <mark>Let me know what you think</mark>, and I'm so sorry again!
sentences.ko: 어느 쪽이든 너 편한 대로 해, 미안하니까 점심이랑 커피는 내가 쏠게! 어떻게 생각하는지 알려줘, 그리고 다시 한번 정말 미안해!
sentences.guide: EIther way, / LUNCH and COFfee are ON ME / to MAKE it up to you! / LET me know what you think, / and I'm SO SORry again!
sentences.tip: [만능 회화 표현] It's on me (내가 쏠게) | Either way (둘 중 어느 쪽이든) | make it up to you (만회하다/신세 갚다)
